rationale: Round 3, ADR-conformance lens. I read 4c46cf64 fresh from disk; this was read-only and needed no checkout. All six of my round-2 asks are ADDRESSED. The revised ADR-0041 amendment text is sound in the main. (1) The undirected `Merge bead/<id>` form is stated honestly. (2) The two `into` forms are pinned to the spec branch. (3) On the fallback path a panel registration never confirms alone, which closes O3's false PASS, pinned by AC-11 (vii). (4) The residual is stated. (5) CLOSE paths stay first-parent. (6) R4.3's reach into the CLOSE paths is stated and argued from Spec-125's admitted evidence, pinned by AC-12 (vii). (7) The binding veto versus audited reattest repair matches the Spec-125 before/after audit discipline. The ADR-0045 Decision 5 transition clause (new staged rules only; existing content grandfathered until step 7; the doctor date check starts with the rule table) and the corrected ADR-0040 and ADR-0044 back-pointers are accurate and consistent with each other. Two narrow ADR-text gaps remain, both fixable in prose. (a) The new fallback ambiguity rule lets an exact (b) or (d) datum break a different-second-parent tie. That departs from FIX-2b and from the Spec-125 amendment's 'fail-closed on every ambiguity' for reattest, and touchpoint (i) does not mention it. The spec also justifies (d) by saying 'the executor writes it only at its own spec-branch merge', which is false: `mindspec reattest` writes bindings too, including on fallback candidates. (b) R6.5's replacement skill line ('proceed on exit 0, otherwise stop') is added after ADR-0045's acceptance, yet the spec says 'No rule is added to any skill'. Under the new Decision 5 transition clause it needs a staged-rule marking or a stated harness-mechanics justification. Neither gap is a false PASS, so I APPROVE with asks.
concrete_changes_required: ADR-0041 amendment (i) / R4.2: price the fallback ambiguity rule. On the fallback path, owned candidates with different second parents are 'resolved iff exactly one second-parent group is exactly corroborated by (b), or by a (d) binding that names a member of that group'. This departs from the FIX-2b rule and from the Spec-125 amendment's reattest 'fail-closed on every ambiguity'. Add it to touchpoint (i) and to the amendment text, scoped to the fallback path, so the AC-18 text-pin covers it.

R4.2 confirmation rule: correct 'The binding is the strongest datum here, because the executor writes it only at its own spec-branch merge'. `mindspec reattest` also writes the binding, including on a fallback candidate after the target-unknown caveat (AC-11 (vii)). Either restrict the fallback's (d) datum (for confirmation and for ambiguity resolution) to an executor-written binding, distinguished by the reattest audit keys, or reword to 'executor-written at merge time, or operator-vouched and audited by reattest'. State that a reattest-written binding then confirms its own candidate on later MF-3 reads, which is the intended audited exit.

R6.5 / Impacted Domains vs ADR-0045 Decision 4/5: the new ms-bead-impl line 'run `mindspec bead ready-check <id>`, proceed on exit 0, otherwise stop and surface its report' is a conditional sequence or rule added to a skill AFTER ADR-0045 is accepted. The spec says 'No rule is added to any skill'. Either classify it explicitly as harness mechanics under Decision 4 (how the harness waits and returns a result), with one sentence of reasoning, or mark it as a staged rule under the Decision 5 transition clause, with its target (`next-action`, spec 133) and a removal date.

findings.title: Revised ADR-0041 amendment, ADR-0045 transition and back-pointers — judged
findings.detail: Undirected form: stated honestly, with no claim of target pinning, and the defence rests on reachability plus exact (b)/(d) plus net effect at the tip. No panel-only fallback confirmation: correct, and it closes O3's reproduced false PASS (AC-11 (vii) returns NoEvidence and MF-3 does not pass). Binding veto: a contradictory binding vetoes automatic identification, and only reattest replaces it after its own checks, with the prior pair audited; this matches the Spec-125 'inspectable audit record ... before/after binding values'. CLOSE paths: R4.2 leaves them first-parent, and R4.3's relaxation only admits Spec-125 item (b)/(c)/(d) exact evidence, so no new close class appears. ADR-0045 Decision 5 transition: coherent; the date check sensibly waits for the rule table that holds the target IDs. ADR-0040 and ADR-0044 back-pointers: accurate and consistent with ADR-0045's Amends line and its Implementation order (the panel brief template lands in specs 130/131, within step 3's '130, 131 and 133').

findings.title: Fallback ambiguity rule is an unpriced departure from FIX-2b / Spec-125 'fail-closed on every ambiguity'
findings.detail: R4.2: 'Owned candidates whose second parents differ are resolved iff exactly one second-parent group is exactly corroborated by (b), or by a (d) binding ... reattest applies the same rule.' The primary path keeps FIX-2b, which always refuses. The Spec-125 amendment says re-attestation is admissible only from an exact match, 'fail-closed on every ambiguity'. A tie broken by a (b) surviving tip is strong evidence. A tie broken by (d) lets agent-writable metadata choose between two genuine subject-named merges; the risk is bounded, since both are real exact merges of X and the net-effect test still runs, but the choice is still made by metadata. ADR touchpoint (i) lists target, defence, residual, revert-awareness and CLOSE, but not this rule.

findings.title: 'Executor writes the binding only at its own spec-branch merge' is inaccurate
findings.detail: R4.2's justification for (d) as 'the strongest datum here' ignores that ReattestLandedMerge writes the same binding keys (reattest.go reattestBindingFn). AC-11 (vii) has reattest nominate exactly the round-1 false-PASS merge with a caveat, so a vouched reattest makes (d) exist and later MF-3 reads confirm it. That is acceptable as the audited operator exit, but the text should say so rather than claim executor-only provenance.

findings.title: New ms-bead-impl line vs ADR-0045 Decision 4/5 and the 'no rule added' claim
findings.detail: R6.5 replaces the override-coverage paragraph with 'run `mindspec bead ready-check <id>`, proceed on exit 0, otherwise stop and surface its report'. Decision 4 bans command sequences and rules ('only after') from skills. Decision 5's new transition clause applies the marking duty to rules staged after acceptance, and this line is written after acceptance. It is arguably harness mechanics ('how this harness ... waits, and returns a result'), but the spec asserts 'No rule is added to any skill' without that reasoning.

findings.title: Selection rule — ADR-lens check
findings.detail: R1.1 now admits `<E>.<N>` beads whose lineage, through the unchanged phase.FindEpicForBead, resolves to E. That includes its `[NNN]` title fallback (verified in derive.go, after the dependency loop). Title prose therefore participates in selection, but only together with the plan-bead ID form, and it is the same lineage function readiness and complete already trust. R1.8 makes the lineage spec the dispatch spec, so another spec's bead cannot be dispatched into S. Spec 124's ADR-0041 fourth-verb preflight is preserved: lineage read errors refuse before mutation. No ADR conflict found; the residual (`readiness.beadIndex` accepts any trailing `.<N>`) is stated and routed to 129b.
